newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T Industries nine month profits up nine percent.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T Industries nine month profits up nine percent.

text.p: B.A.T Industries reported on Wednesday a nine percent rise in pretax profits on Wednesday to 2.039 billion pounds ($3.28 billion) in the last nine months and insisted the company has never kept from the public any conclusions showing that smoking causes diseases.

"I would like to reassure shareholders that there has never been any concealment from the public of any conclusions establishing that smoking causes diseases," chairman Lord Cairns said. "Indeed, the (tobacco) companies continue to support independent research without any restriction on publication," said Cairns. ($1=.6223 Pound)
B.A.T Industries nine month profits up nine percent
The growing pace of litigation claims against the company's U.S. tocacco subsidiary Brown & Williamson, and the U.S. industry in general, continues to unsettle investors and hurt B.A.T's share price.

B.A.T reported a trading profit of 846 million pounds, up three percent, from its financial services division. The general business profit was slightly up at 502 milion pounds, with growth at Farmers more than compensating for a deterioration in British insurer Eagle Star.
The life and investment business reported a five percent increase in profit to 344 million pounds in the nine months to September 30.
A total trading profit from tobacco of 1.265 billion pounds showed steady growth of seven percent compared to last year's record result.
Overall group cigarette volumes were up three percent, with strong sales growth in the Asia Pacific and Amesca regions, said the company.
